_link.title: I can identify the three types of neurons and describe the direction in which each transmits neural messages

toLevel2.stem: Which type of neuron transmits messages from the PNS to the CNS?
Which type of neuron transmits messages from the CNS to the PNS?

toLevel2.answer: In the brain and spinal cord

toLevel2.stem: What is the function of interneurons?
toLevel2.answer: They transfer messages between sensory and motor neurons
distractors: They detect stimuli from the external environment
They carry commands to the skeletal muscles directly
They transmit messages from the PNS to the CNS only

toLevel2.stem: What is another name for sensory neurons?
Sensory neurons transmit messages about bodily sensations from the PNS to the CNS.
Motor neurons transmit messages from the PNS to the CNS.
Sensory neurons transmit messages {{blank:1}} the CNS, while motor neurons transmit messages {{blank:2}} the CNS.
Interneurons are found in the {{blank:1}} and spinal cord, where they transfer messages between sensory and motor neurons.
Motor neurons are also known as {{blank:1}} neurons because they carry messages away from the CNS.

toLevel3.stem: Why is it important to know the direction each neuron type transmits?
toLevel3.answer: It is necessary for accurately describing conscious responses and reflexes
distractors: Direction is only relevant for neuroscience research, not VCE exams
All neurons transmit in the same direction so it does not matter
Direction only matters for motor neurons, not sensory or interneurons

toLevel3.stem: How do the three neuron types work together during a spinal reflex?
toLevel3.answer: Sensory neurons detect, interneurons relay, motor neurons produce the response
distractors: Motor neurons detect, interneurons relay, sensory neurons respond to danger
Interneurons detect, sensory neurons relay, motor neurons produce the response
All three types perform the same function at different speeds during reflexes

toLevel3.stem: Why are sensory neurons described as 'afferent'?
toLevel3.answer: They carry messages toward the CNS
distractors: They carry messages away from the CNS
They are found within the spinal cord
They produce the motor response output

toLevel3.stem: Why are motor neurons described as 'efferent'?
toLevel3.answer: They carry messages away from the CNS
distractors: They carry messages toward the CNS
They detect stimuli from the environment
They are located in the brain and cord

toLevel3.stem: What is the relationship between interneurons and the CNS?
toLevel3.answer: Interneurons make up the brain and spinal cord
distractors: Interneurons are found in the PNS only
Interneurons are located in skeletal muscles
Interneurons exist outside the nervous system

toLevel3.stem: Why do interneurons need to connect sensory and motor neurons?
toLevel3.answer: Sensory neurons detect stimuli; motor neurons produce responses; interneurons bridge them
distractors: Sensory and motor neurons are identical and do not need a bridge between them
Interneurons replace sensory and motor neurons once the signal reaches the CNS
Motor neurons can directly connect to sensory neurons without any intermediary

toLevel3.stem: In a spinal reflex, sensory neurons carry the signal to the spinal cord, interneurons relay it, and motor neurons carry the response to skeletal muscles.
The term 'afferent' means carrying messages {{blank:1}} the CNS, while 'efferent' means carrying messages {{blank:2}} the CNS.
Interneurons connect sensory and motor neurons by {{blank:1}} messages within the brain and spinal cord.
During a spinal reflex, the pain signal is carried to the spinal cord by {{blank:1}} neurons and the withdrawal command is carried to muscles by {{blank:2}} neurons.

toLevel4.stem: Ava touches a hot pan and her hand jerks away. Which neuron type carried the pain signal from her skin to her spinal cord?
In Ava's spinal reflex, which neuron type carried the withdrawal command to her arm muscles?
A student writes: 'Motor neurons carry the pain signal to the spinal cord.' How should this be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: Sensory neurons carry messages to the spinal cord, not motor neurons
distractors: The statement is correct and does not need any correction at all
Interneurons carry the pain signal to the spinal cord, not motor neurons
Motor neurons carry pain signals but only during conscious responses

toLevel4.stem: Tom is asked which neuron type relays information within the spinal cord during a reflex. Which answer is correct?
A diagram shows a neural pathway from a receptor in the foot to the brain. Which neuron type would be labelled inside the spinal cord?
Ella decides to pick up a pen from her desk. Which neuron type carries the movement command from her CNS to her arm muscles?
A VCE exam question asks: 'Name the neuron type that transmits messages about bodily sensations to the CNS.' Which answer is correct?
When Ava touches a hot pan, {{blank:1}} neurons carry the pain signal to the spinal cord, and {{blank:2}} neurons carry the withdrawal command to her muscles.
Inside the spinal cord, {{blank:1}} relay the signal from the sensory neuron to the motor neuron during a reflex.
When Ella decides to pick up a pen, the movement command is carried from the CNS to her arm muscles by {{blank:1}} neurons.

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that sensory neurons are found in the spinal cord because they carry signals there. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sensory neurons are in the PNS and carry signals to the cord, not within it
distractors: Correct; sensory neurons are located wherever they carry their signals to
Correct; the spinal cord contains all three types of neurons equally
Incorrect; sensory neurons do not carry any signals to the spinal cord

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee argues that interneurons are unnecessary because sensory neurons could connect directly to motor neurons. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; interneurons enable processing and integration of information
distractors: Correct; direct connections would be faster and more effective overall
Correct; interneurons serve no functional purpose in the nervous system
Incorrect; sensory neurons and motor neurons are the same type of cell

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that motor neurons carry messages 'to the CNS.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; motor neurons carry messages away from the CNS to the PNS
distractors: Correct; motor neurons transmit messages in both possible directions
Correct; motor neurons carry messages to the CNS for processing there
Incorrect; motor neurons do not transmit any messages in any direction

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that knowing the direction of neural transmission is irrelevant to VCE Psychology. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; direction is essential for describing responses and reflexes accurately
distractors: Correct; direction is never assessed in any VCE Psychology exam questions
Correct; all neurons transmit in the same direction so it is not important
Incorrect; direction is only relevant for interneurons, not other neuron types

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that all three neuron types are found equally in both the CNS and PNS. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the CNS contains interneurons while the PNS has sensory and motor neurons
distractors: Correct; all neuron types are distributed evenly across the entire nervous system
Correct; there is no distinction between where different neuron types are located
Incorrect; all three neuron types are found only in the CNS, never the PNS

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that interneurons should be classified as part of the PNS because they connect to PNS neurons. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; interneurons are in the CNS regardless of their connections to PNS neurons
distractors: Correct; connecting to PNS neurons makes interneurons part of the PNS system
Correct; the location of connections determines which division a neuron belongs to
Incorrect; interneurons have no connections to any neurons in the PNS at all

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that afferent and efferent are just alternative names with no functional meaning. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; afferent means toward the CNS and efferent means away from the CNS
distractors: Correct; the terms are interchangeable and carry no directional meaning
Correct; both terms simply mean the same thing as the word neuron itself
Incorrect; afferent means away from the CNS and efferent means toward it

toLevel5.stem: A textbook states that 'motor neurons detect stimuli and carry signals to the brain.' Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sensory neurons detect stimuli and carry signals toward the CNS
distractors: Correct; motor neurons detect stimuli and carry signals to the brain always
Correct; detecting stimuli is a function shared by all three neuron types
Incorrect; no neuron type is responsible for detecting stimuli from the body

toLevel5.stem: The claim that sensory neurons are in the spinal cord is {{blank:1}} because sensory neurons are located in the {{blank:2}}.
The claim that direction of transmission is irrelevant is {{blank:1}} because it is essential for accurately describing {{blank:2}} and reflexes.
